title: Congress split over Middle East - NewsBreak
text: WASHINGTON (NEXSTAR) – A somewhat surprising split is emerging on Capitol Hill as lawmakers weigh in on potential U.S. involvement in the conflict in the Middle East. The arguments about whether or not to have the U.S. military play a role are not divided by party. Plus, many in Congress are pushing to have some say in whether America joins in Israel’s fight against Iran. Republican Senator Josh Hawley says U.S. troops should stay out of the conflict. “I don’t want to see there be a MidEast war. I don’t want the United States to be involved in it. I don’t want to see us be bombing,” Hawley said. Not all Republicans agree. Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas.) supports the possibility of the U.S. military joining Israel’s bombing campaign to prevent Iran from getting nuclear weapons. “The President may well authorize a limited bombing strike to take out that one nuclear weapons facility in the basement of a mountain in Fordow. And if he does so, it will make Americans substantially safer,” Cruz said. Democratic Senator John Fetterman says he’d support a U.S. strike on Iran too. “It’s like clearly they’re trying to build a bomb. We can’t ever allow that. We have an opportunity to take it out. Clearly we should all do that. We have the capabilities to do that,” Fetterman said. Democratic Senator Tim Kaine disagrees. “U.S. war with Iran right now would be completely unnecessary, and likely over time really deepen catastrophic consequences,” Kaine said. President Trump says he’s keeping his options open and hasn’t decided how to move forward. Democratic Senator Mark Warner says that’s part of the problem, arguing the Trump Administration isn’t being transparent enough with lawmakers. “What so concerns me is I have no idea what the Administration’s policy is on this conflict,” Warner said. Senator Kaine argues Congress should get a say in what happens next. He’s leading a war powers resolution to block President Trump from using U.S. military force against Iran without a vote in Congress. “We shouldn’t go to war with Iran without a Congressional debate and vote,” Kaine said. There’s similar legislation being introduced in the House with support from both parties. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WGN-TV.
